lines: What if... one morning, every gun in the world just vanished?
It's nine a.m. on an ordinary Tuesday.
Across the planet, there are more than a billion guns.
In homes, on police belts, at army bases, and stacked in warehouses.
Then, in a single instant...
Poof.
Every single one of them disappears.
At first, almost nobody notices.
A police officer reaches for an empty holster.
A hunter stares down at empty hands.
And a soldier on patrol looks down... at nothing.
Within an hour, the news explodes.
Phones light up all over the world.
Scientists have no explanation.
And governments call emergency meetings.
The world splits into two moods.
Some people celebrate in the streets.
Others suddenly feel unsafe, like farmers far from help, or shop owners who kept a gun behind the counter.
The first few days are chaotic.
Some criminals try to take advantage... but they're unarmed too.
Police switch to batons, pepper spray, and tasers.
And stores sell out of baseball bats, locks, and security cameras.
Armies are hit the hardest.
Rifles, machine guns, and tank cannons are all gone.
But missiles and drones still exist, so the world's superpowers nervously watch each other.
Here's the twist. The knowledge to make guns didn't vanish.
Factories could start building them again within weeks.
So world leaders rush to the United Nations.
Many countries agree to stop making new guns.
But not everyone signs.
Over the next year, some things get much better.
Around two hundred and fifty thousand people die from guns every year. That number drops toward zero.
Mass shootings stop. Accidental shootings at home stop.
Kids worry less at school, and more people feel safe walking at night.
But it's not all good news.
Crime doesn't disappear. People turn to knives and other weapons.
Farmers lose a way to protect their animals from wolves and coyotes.
Deer and wild boar populations grow fast without hunters.
Gun factory workers lose their jobs overnight.
And in a fight, the biggest and strongest now have the advantage.
Meanwhile, something unexpected happens.
Bows and crossbows make a huge comeback.
Archery shops can't keep anything on the shelves.
Some wars slow to a crawl.
Without guns, holding territory is much harder.
Peacekeepers move in, and cease-fires start to stick.
Five years later, the world looks different.
In many countries, police work mostly unarmed, like they already do in Britain and Iceland.
Museums display old photos of guns, and kids ask what they were like.
So here's the big question.
Would humanity rebuild them...
or choose to keep a world without guns?
What do you think?
